Article 13
P2TP2A as an independent institution in the region must be in one coordination together with BKKBD whose scope of duties and responsibilities includes, among others, the field of protection of women, children and gender mainstreaming.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Rejang Lebong Regency. 2. Regional Government is the administration of governmental affairs by the regional government and the Regional House of Representatives according to the principles of autonomy and assistance tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy within the system and principles of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. 3. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administrator who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Regent is the Regent of Rejang Lebong. 5. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the Regional House of Representatives of Rejang Lebong Regency. 6. Regional Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is the Regional Work Unit of Rejang Lebong Regency. 7. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent in the administration of regional government consisting of regional secretariat, DPRD secretariat, regional agencies, regional technical institutions, sub-districts, and urban villages. 8. Regional Population and Family Planning Agency, hereinafter abbreviated as BKKBD, is the Regional Population and Family Planning Agency of Rejang Lebong Regency. 9. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a child still in the womb. 10. Woman is an adult human being of female gender and a person recognized by law as a woman. 11. Prevention is activities carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children. 12. Protection is all service actions to guarantee and protect the rights of victims of acts of violence organized by the Integrated Service Center. 13. Violence is any act that results in or causes misery and suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological including neglect, threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or in private life. 14. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage or unconsciousness and/or causes death. 15. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, lack of confidence or severe psychological suffering to a person. 16. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual relations, whether unnatural or unwanted with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 17. Exploitation is an action with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial. 18. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 19. Victim of acts of violence is an individual or group of people who experience physical, mental or emotional suffering, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or regional government apparatus or by individuals. 20. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 21. Assistance is activities and actions carried out by assistants during the service process. 22. Assistant is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance. 23. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of acts of violence to their family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfill their needs. 24. Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims from psychosocial disorders and restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in society. 25. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, community, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection. 26. Institution is an agency/service/body/office within the scope of the regional government and/or a non-governmental organization (NGO) that conducts assistance. 27. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an integrated service unit established by the regional government to provide services in the context of empowerment of Women and Children victims of acts of violence. 28. Regional Action Plan, hereinafter abbreviated as RAD, is a basis and guideline for related agencies, vertical institutions, and the community, in carrying out activities for the implementation of prevention and protection of women and children victims of acts of violence. 29. Safe House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards. 30. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations. 31. Family is a person who has a blood relationship in a straight line upward or downward and collateral line up to the third degree, or who has a marital relationship, or a person who is a dependent of a woman and/or child. 32. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 33.

Article 25
(1) The Regional Government establishes partnerships with the business sector for support in the implementation of protection for women and children in the regional area.
(2) The partnership as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out through:
   a. notification of employment opportunity information for women victims of violence;
   b. education and training for women victims of violence;
   c. educational assistance for women and children victims of violence who have been withdrawn from their education; and
   d. fostering and increasing economic independence of women victims of violence.
(3) The partnership as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) shall be set forth in the form of an agreement.

CHAPTER XIV
SPECIAL PROVISIONS
Article 32
(1) The handling of legal cases in the investigation process by law enforcement officials must be handled by special investigators who have been appointed according to their competence by law enforcement institutions for the field of protection of women and children.
(2) Special investigators as referred to in paragraph (1) are:
a. in cases of investigation for women or girl victims of violence must be handled by female investigators;
b. the implementation process as referred to in letter a must be in a closed room attended only by the victim's parents or guardian together with the advocacy and psychology team from P2TP2A who have the same gender;
c. in cases of investigation for boy victims of violence may be conducted by male or female investigators, preferably of the same gender and implemented as referred to in letter b; and
d. The trial process is not open to the public.

CHAPTER XIII
SANCTION PROVISIONS
Article 31
(1) Every person who intentionally fails to provide protection to women and children resulting in the occurrence of acts of violence, allows acts of violence to occur, and/or does not report and does not provide protection to victims, shall be subject to sanctions as stipulated in the Laws and Regulations.
(2) Officials appointed to administer protection who fail to carry out their obligations and responsibilities shall be subject to sanctions in accordance with the provisions of the Laws and Regulations.
(3) P2TP2A administrators who carry out service and protection duties for Children and Women from acts of violence and violate service principles may be subject to sanctions in accordance with the internal mechanisms of the P2TP2A organization.

Considering : a. that in order to guarantee the rights of women and children to participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and to receive protection from violence, discrimination and other violations of the rights of women and children, it is necessary to undertake efforts to prevent and handle violence against women and children. b. that in order for the efforts to prevent and handle violence against women and children to obtain optimal results, and to be implemented quickly, in a planned, integrated, comprehensive and organized manner by involving all related elements in the region, it is necessary to have regulations concerning the prevention and handling of violence against women and children who are victims of violence. c. that based on the considerations as referred to in letters a and b, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Prevention and Handling of Violence Against Women and Children. Law Number 21 Year 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Criminal Act of Trafficking in Persons (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Year 2007 Number 58, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 4720); 12. Law Number 36 Year 2009 concerning Health (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Year 2009 Number 99, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 3495); 13. Law Number 12 Year 2011 concerning the Formation of Laws and Regulations (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Year 2011 Number 82, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 5234); 14. Law Number 23 Year 2014 concerning Regional Government as amended several times most recently by Law Number 9 Year 2015 (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Year 2015 Number 2016, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 58); 15. Presidential Decree Number 181 year 1998 concerning the National Commission on Anti-Violence Against Women; 20.

CHAPTER IX
REGIONAL ACTION PLAN
Article 26
(1) In order to implement obligations and responsibilities, the regional government establishes action programs and activities for the protection of women and children in 1 (one) RAD as the basis for implementing protection of women and children from acts of violence.
(2) RAD as referred to in paragraph (1), constitutes part of the Regional Medium-Term Development Plan.
(3) Further provisions regarding RAD as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be regulated by the Regent's Regulation.

Article 18
The form of services provided to women and children victims of violence, exploitation, human trafficking or neglect shall be implemented in accordance with the rights of victims as referred to in Article 6.

Article 3
The regulation of the implementation of prevention and handling of violence against women and children is intended to provide protection and services for women and children victims of acts of violence.

CHAPTER X
GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION
Article 27
(1) The Regent conducts guidance and supervision of the implementation of protection of women and children from acts of violence.
(2) Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1), includes: a. guidelines and fulfillment standards;
b. technical guidance and training;
c. provision of facilities;
d. monitoring; and
e. evaluation.
(3) Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1), is conducted with the principles of:
a. professional;
b. transparent; and
c. accountable.
(4) Guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (2) and paragraph (3), are in order to realize the objectives of implementing protection of women and children from acts of violence in accordance with minimum service standards implemented by SKPD/UKPD and the community.
(5) The Regent may appoint BKKBD whose scope of duties and responsibilities includes protection of women and children to conduct guidance and supervision.

Article 11
(1) In order to carry out activities for the prevention and handling of violence against women and children, the Regional Government establishes P2TP2A as an integrated service center for women and children who are victims of acts of violence.
(2) P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (1) is established on a joint initiative between the Regional Government, NGOs, Universities, professional organizations, organizations, and the community.
(3) The institutional structure of P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (2) is determined by a Regent’s Decree.
(4) Further provisions regarding the organization of P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (1) are regulated by a Regent’s Regulation.

Article 28
The community may conduct supervision of the implementation of protection for women and children from acts of violence organized by the regional government, through a mechanism of conveying aspirations to the Regent or DPRD.

CHAPTER V
OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES
Article 7
Obligations and responsibilities in conducting prevention and mitigation in the form of protection and services for women and children from acts of violence are the shared responsibility of:
a. regional government;
b. community;
c. family; and
d. parents.

Article 22
Further provisions regarding the procedures for service delivery in handling the protection of women and children victims of violence as well as the operational standards as referred to in Article 18 and Article 20, shall be regulated by a Regent Regulation.

2.4.rationale: In the original Indonesian text, Pasal 13 states: “P2TP2A ... harus berada dalam satu koordinasi bersama dengan BKKBD yang lingkup tugas dan tanggungjawabnya diantaranya meliputi bidang perlindungan perempuan, anak dan pengarusutamaan gender.” This only says BKKBD’s scope includes gender mainstreaming (pengarusutamaan gender) and that P2TP2A coordinates with BKKBD. It does not establish a gender-mainstreaming institutionalisation mechanism within this regulation (e.g., a mandated gender mainstreaming unit, gender focal points across SKPD, gender budgeting, gender analysis requirements, or mainstreaming across all sectors). The judge over-interpreted a mention of ‘gender mainstreaming’ in BKKBD’s remit as sufficient institutionalisation, leading to a false positive. The English passage is consistent with the Indonesian, so this is not a translation issue, and the relevant passage was retrieved.

(1) In order to implement obligations and responsibilities, the regional government establishes action programs and activities for the protection of women and children in 1 (one) RAD as the basis for implementing protection of women and children from acts of violence.
(2) RAD as referred to in paragraph (1), constitutes part of the Regional Medium-Term Development Plan.
(3) Further provisions regarding RAD as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be regulated by the Regent's Regulation.

Article 28
The community may conduct supervision of the implementation of protection for women and children from acts of violence organized by the regional government, through a mechanism of conveying aspirations to the Regent or DPRD.

4.4.rationale: The original Indonesian text explicitly includes education/awareness activities as prevention measures. Pasal 17 ayat (1) lists forms of prevention including: (a) “kegiatan sosialisasi peraturan perundang-undangan ... kepada masyarakat luas” and (g) “penyuluhan/sosialisasi dalam bentuk penyadaran masyarakat luas ... khususnya para orang tua untuk melindungi perempuan dan anak.” These are clearly prevention-through-education/socialization/counseling provisions. The retrieved English candidates accurately reflect this content, and the judge’s rationale matches the Indonesian. Therefore the golden label ‘No’ appears incorrect; it should be ‘Yes’ given Pasal 17.
